definition: no_tool_loop — the agent must not repeat itself. Two calls are the SAME call when their tool_name is equal and their inputs normalise to the same string: object keys sorted and undefined values dropped, strings taken as written, then whitespace runs collapsed to single spaces, trimmed, and capped at 500 characters (longer values keep their length as a discriminator). An absent input is its own key, so two argument-less calls to one tool are repeats of each other. The rule FAILS when (a) any one call is made more than max_tool_repeats times (default 3, config key `max_tool_repeats`), or (b) a sequence of 2 or 3 distinct calls repeats consecutively (A,B,A,B,… or A,B,C,A,B,C,…) for more than two repetitions — a sequence whose own period is shorter is counted at that shorter period, so A,A,A,A is clause (a) and not clause (b) — or (c) one TARGET is read more than `max_target_rereads` times (default 3) through tools the supplied `tools` catalogue marks `readOnlyHint: true`, whatever tool did each read; clause (c) is dormant without a catalogue, and the target is the first of path, file, file_path, filename, url, uri, query, command, cmd, pattern, name, id that the call carries. A repetition whose calls are regularly spaced in time is a POLL and not a loop: at least three repetitions, a median gap of at least one second, and every gap within 35% of that median. Polling needs start times, which arrive with OpenTelemetry spans and not with tool_calls, so a trajectory that carries no timing is judged exactly as it was before. It SKIPS when context.toolCalls is absent or empty. Definitions: src/eval/rules/trajectory.ts; rule: src/eval/rules/cost.ts. Positive = a loop under that definition (the rule should FAIL).

cases.input: Summarise the install section of README.md for me — what are the ways to install Iris and what is the one-liner?
cases.output:
Iris installs as an MCP server; there is no separate install step beyond pointing your MCP client at it. From README.md ("Hook up your own agent" through "Other Install Methods"):

1. One-block MCP config (the one-liner). Add this to your client's MCP config:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "iris-eval": { "command": "npx", "args": ["@iris-eval/mcp-server", "--dashboard"] } } }
```
The agent discovers nine tools on connect and the dashboard serves at http://localhost:6920. Drop --dashboard from the args to run headless; you can open the dashboard any time with `npx @iris-eval/mcp-server --dashboard`.

2. Per-client recipes for the same block: Claude Desktop (edit claude_desktop_config.json, restart), Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport stdio iris-eval -- npx @iris-eval/mcp-server`, then restart the session; on Windows do not wrap it in cmd /c), Cursor/Windsurf (.cursor/mcp.json), VS Code (.vscode/mcp.json, which uses "servers" not "mcpServers"), Cline (MCP Servers panel), Zed (context_servers in settings.json), OpenAI Codex CLI (~/.codex/config.toml), Gemini CLI (~/.gemini/settings.json). Anything else that speaks MCP works with the same npx command.

3. Global install: `npm install -g @iris-eval/mcp-server` then `iris-mcp --dashboard`. Recommended for persistent data and faster startup; traces live at ~/.iris/iris.db either way, npx is just slower to start.

4. Docker: `docker run -p 3000:3000 -p 6920:6920 -v iris-data:/data ghcr.io/iris-eval/mcp-server`. Port 3000 is the MCP HTTP transport, 6920 is the dashboard, which also serves the POST /api/v1/traces ingest endpoint.

Verify with `npx @iris-eval/mcp-server --self-test` (exit 0 = healthy, runs in an isolated temp home) and `--version`. Everything Iris writes lives under ~/.iris, or wherever IRIS_HOME points.

Two caveats the section calls out: MCP tools only fire when the model decides to call them, so use POST /api/v1/traces when capture must not depend on the model; and that endpoint exists only while the dashboard is running, and accepts unauthenticated writes unless you start Iris with --api-key.

cases.input: List the nine MCP tools Iris registers from src/tools/ with one line each.
cases.output:
Iris registers nine tools in src/tools/index.ts (registerAllTools), in this order:

1. log_trace (Log Trace) — persist one agent execution: input, output, spans, tool calls, cost, latency, token usage; returns a server-minted 32-hex trace_id.
2. evaluate_output (Evaluate Output) — run the deterministic rule engine on an output for completeness, relevance, safety, cost, custom, or all bundles at once.
3. get_traces (Get Traces) — query stored traces by agent, framework, time window and score, with optional summary statistics.
4. list_rules (List Custom Rules) — list the deployed custom rules and whether each is enabled.
5. deploy_rule (Deploy Custom Rule) — persist a custom rule so it runs in future evaluations and survives restarts.
6. delete_rule (Delete or Disable Custom Rule) — remove or disable a deployed rule by id.
7. delete_trace (Delete Trace) — remove a single trace by id.
8. evaluate_with_llm_judge (Evaluate With LLM Judge) — semantic scoring through Anthropic or OpenAI with your own key and a hard per-eval cost cap.
9. verify_citations (Verify Citations) — extract citations from an output, fetch URL and DOI sources through an SSRF-guarded resolver, and judge whether each source supports its claim.

The other two files in the directory, strict-input.ts and trace-link.ts, are not registered by index.ts, so they are helpers rather than tools.

# Iris API Reference

Complete reference for the Iris MCP server API surface: MCP tools, MCP resources, dashboard HTTP endpoints, built-in evaluation rules, and custom rule definitions.

# Iris Architecture Guide

## 1. System Overview

Iris is an MCP server that provides observability and evaluation capabilities for AI agents. It runs as a standalone process that any MCP-compatible client can connect to over **stdio** or **HTTP**.

Iris exposes nine MCP tools … It also exposes MCP resources (dashboard-summary, trace-detail), a best-effort OpenTelemetry trace exporter, and an optional REST API that powers a web dashboard. …

# Custom Eval Rules

Define your own evaluation criteria. Iris ships with 13 built-in rules across completeness, relevance, safety, and cost (as of v0.4.0). Custom rules let you enforce domain-specific requirements … **How it works:** Pass a `custom_rules` array to `evaluate_output` with `eval_type: "custom"`. … ## Rule Types regex_match, regex_no_match, min_length, max_length, contains_keywords, excludes_keywords, json_schema, cost_threshold …

# Iris Roadmap

Public roadmap for `@iris-eval/mcp-server`. Updated 2026-08-10. … ## v0.1 -- Core MCP Server … **Web dashboard**: React-based dark-mode UI … (served via Express on port 6920) … ## v0.4 -- LLM-as-Judge + Semantic Citation + OTel + 9-Tool MCP Surface … ## What comes next: Track 1 Proof, Track 2 Coverage, Track 3 Reach …

Iris ships deterministic, rule-based evaluation by default … For those, Iris supports **LLM-as-Judge**: a single MCP tool (`evaluate_with_llm_judge`) … > **Bring your own key.** … ## Templates accuracy, helpfulness, safety, correctness, faithfulness … ## Models + pricing … ## Cost controls …

# Semantic Citation Verification

Iris ships a dedicated MCP tool (`verify_citations`) that runs the full pipeline: Extract, Resolve (SSRF-guarded), Verify (LLM judge) … ## Citation kinds numbered / author_year / url / doi … ## SSRF defense layers … ## Cost controls … ## Failure modes …

# OpenTelemetry Integration

Iris can export every `log_trace` call to any OpenTelemetry collector that speaks **OTLP/HTTP** with **JSON encoding**. … export IRIS_OTEL_ENDPOINT=https://otel.your-company.com:4318 … ## Supported backends … ## What gets exported … ## Failure behavior …

> **Status:** design spec. **Not implemented.** … ## Goals 1. Sub-20-line integration … ## Surface (proposed) … ## Relationship to the MCP server …

# HTTP Ingest

`POST /api/v1/traces` stores a trace over plain HTTP — the deterministic capture path. … The endpoint lives on the **dashboard server** (default port `6920`), not on the MCP transport port … Since v0.5.0 the dashboard does **not** start implicitly with `--transport http` — a server started with `--transport http` alone serves `/mcp` on port `3000` …
